resources.string: Currently %1$s - Move keyboard cycles through these

Center is one full-width keyboard. Dual puts two full copies side by side. Split cuts the key grid in half and duplicates the middle column when the column count is odd (on Suave, only the center column is duplicated). Left and Right stay hidden here until they park a narrower keyboard.
On - Dual is skipped when two copies would make keys narrower than %1$d dp
Off - Dual is used even when keys would be squeezed
On a phone in portrait, two full copies of a 5-column layout become too skinny to type on. Turn this off if you still want Dual on a narrow screen.
On - Split is skipped when the screen is taller than it is wide
Off - Split is used whenever it is enabled

Split parks two halves on the left and right. In portrait there is no room between them, so Move keyboard skips Split. Landscape keeps it. Dual has its own cramped check. Turn this off to cycle Split in portrait too.
On - a notice names the layout or position after you switch
Off - switching layout or position stays silent
The notice overlays the keys and does not change keyboard height. It names the layout after Switch language, or the position after Move keyboard.
On - a notice confirms after a successful copy
The notice overlays the keys and does not change keyboard height. It appears only after copy succeeds. Editors that handle copy themselves, such as some terminals, do not show it.
On - a notice confirms after a successful cut
The notice overlays the keys and does not change keyboard height. It appears only after cut succeeds. Editors that handle cut themselves, such as some terminals, do not show it.

On - Bitwarden and other Autofill services can show chips above the keyboard
Off - Autofill stays in the system dropdown instead of this keyboard

This uses Android Autofill. Set Bitwarden as the Autofill service in system settings, and in Bitwarden set Display autofill suggestions to Inline (not Popup). Popup and keyboard chips are mutually exclusive there. Chrome also needs Autofill using another service. Tap a chip to fill. Swipe right on space fills the top (non-logo) chip. The keyboard never sees the password. Debug af=wait / 0 / N is Android asked / no chips / N chips on this keyboard.
Currently %1$d dp - height of the strip above the keys
On - letter keys and control keys use different background colors
Off - every key uses the same background color
Letters, numbers, and symbols use the theme surface. Space, modifiers, 123, Enter, and similar controls use the variant fill.
On - %1$s when a key is tapped
Requires touch feedback to be enabled in your device\'s system settings, or this has no effect regardless of this toggle.
On - %1$s when a swipe on a key locks in
Off - no vibration when a swipe locks in
This is the moment a key swipe is recognized. Sliding on space or backspace is Vibrate for slides.
On - %1$s when sliding on space or backspace
Requires touch feedback to be enabled in your device\'s system settings, or this has no effect regardless of this toggle.
On - %1$s when hold-repeat starts on a key or a settings plus/minus
Off - holding to repeat does not vibrate
Requires touch feedback in your device\'s system settings, or this has no effect. The first tap still follows Vibrate on tap; this switch is only the repeating that follows a hold.
On - %1$s when Shift, Ctrl, Alt, or Esc engage or release
Distinct from a letter tap so a held or locked modifier is felt, not just seen.
Currently %1$s key-heights - same height as the key grid
Currently %1$s key-heights - %2$s extra above the keys for this layer\'s content

Every layer has a height in key-heights. Taller than the key grid leaves space above the keys; that space is the layer\'s content area (the emoji picker on emoji, the clipboard list on clipboard, empty on layers with no content). Reset restores the layout default.
Currently %1$spx - how far a touch must move before it counts as a swipe instead of a tap
Spacebar: Allow normal swipes to work with slide gestures
Backspace: Allow normal swipes to work with slide gestures
Are you sure you want to reset settings to defaults?
On - keys show no letter labels
Off - keys show their letter labels
On - keys show no symbol labels
Off - keys show their symbol labels
On - keys show no number labels
Off - keys show their number labels
On - keys show no modifier labels
Off - keys show their modifier labels
On - keys show no layer-switch labels
Off - keys show their layer-switch labels
On - keys show no special-action labels
Off - keys show their special-action labels
On - keys show no arrow labels
Off - keys show their arrow labels
On - keys show no editing labels
Off - keys show their editing labels
Hiding a category removes its labels and icons from the keys. The keys themselves still work.

The hide key on the keyboard writes the same Appearance switches as the hide-letter rows. It only changes the groups you select here. Groups you leave unselected stay as they are. If any selected group is visible, the key hides all of them. If they are all already hidden, the key shows them again.
On - the keycap fill flashes while your finger is down
Off - the keycap keeps its normal fill while pressed
While a key is held, its background switches to the theme press color. This is the whole keycap, not the letter.
On - the keycap flashes after you type a character
Off - the keycap does not flash after a character
After a character is typed, the key fills with a brief overlay and fades. Commands such as Backspace do not trigger it. Password fields never show it.
On - the typed character drops down the key and fades
Off - no extra letter appears on the key after typing
After a character is typed, a copy of that character slides down the keycap and fades. Only typed text, not commands. Password fields never show it.
On - fills the area behind the keys with the theme background color
Off - keys sit on the transparent IME window
Currently %1$sdp padding on the left and right of each key
Currently 0dp - keys in a row sit flush
Currently %1$sdp padding above and below each key
The visible gap between two keys is twice this value, because each key brings its own padding. Horizontal and vertical are independent.
Currently none - keys have no outline
Thumb-Key stored this in tenths of a dp, so 10 is a 1dp line. 0 turns the outline off.
Currently %1$s%% - corners scale with key size
Currently %1$sdp of extra space below the keys
Currently 0dp - keys sit at the bottom of the keyboard area
Extra empty space below the keys. This is not the system gesture inset - that is Ignore bottom padding.
Access hidden symbol keys without switching to numeric view
Slide and hold to repeat cursor movement, slide-return-hold for word movement. Backspace: slide-hold to repeat delete, slide-return-hold for word delete.
On - a quick tap queues Esc as a Meta-via-Escape combo for the next key; tapping Esc again while queued sends a real Escape instead
Off - Esc always just sends a real Escape, with no combo behavior

\"Meta via Escape\" is a standard terminal convention (Emacs and most terminals treat \"Esc x\" as \"M-x\"), which is what lets Esc double as a modifier here. Holding Esc while typing other keys sends that combo for as long as it\'s held; a quick tap queues it for just the next key. Tapping Esc again while it\'s still queued (Esc+Esc) sends a plain Escape instead of silently clearing the queue - the escape hatch for when you actually just wanted to press Escape.
On - a quick tap queues Ctrl for the next key; hold keeps it active across several keys
Off - Ctrl always just sends a Ctrl key event, with no combo behavior

When on, tap is one-shot (C-x) and hold stays active while the key is down (C-x then C-s without re-tapping Ctrl). When off, this key always sends the actual Ctrl key, like any other command, including repeat-on-hold.
On - a quick tap queues Alt for the next key; hold keeps it active across several keys
Off - Alt always just sends an Alt key event, with no combo behavior
Same activation shape as Ctrl: tap is one-shot, hold stays active while down. When off, this key always sends the actual Alt key.
On - a quick tap capitalizes the next character; hold is caps lock until tapped off
Off - Shift always just sends a Shift key event, with no combo behavior
When on, tap is one-shot capitalization and a genuine hold locks caps until Shift is tapped again. When off, this key always sends the actual Shift key.
Warning: This will clear out your current database
On - the keyboard extends into the bottom system inset (e.g. behind gesture navigation)
Off - the keyboard leaves room for the bottom system inset
On - the keyboard never takes over the full screen, even in landscape
Off - the keyboard may switch to a fullscreen editor in some apps/orientations

Some apps ask the keyboard to take over the whole screen (usually in landscape) so there\'s room to type, hiding the app\'s own content until you\'re done. Turning this on keeps the normal keyboard layout visible instead, at the cost of less room to see what you\'re typing into.
Mode \"%s\" is not defined for layout \"%s\".
On - stores copied text and images for quick access
Off - copied text and images aren\'t stored for later
On - old unpinned clips are removed automatically
Off - clips stay in history until you remove them
Currently cleans up unpinned clips after %1$s
On - oldest clips are removed once the limit is reached
Off - clipboard history can grow without limit
On - copies go to Suave\'s internal clipboard instead of the system clipboard
Off - copies go to the normal system clipboard, shared with every app

The system clipboard is shared across every app on the device, and some apps or accessibility services can read it. Suave\'s private clipboard is only ever accessible from this keyboard, at the cost of not being able to paste what you copied here into another keyboard or clipboard manager.
On - copies from other apps, including images, are stored in Suave\'s history
Off - only copies made from this keyboard are stored

Suave cannot read Samsung\'s existing clipboard panel. While this is on and Suave is the keyboard, new system copies (text and images) are recorded into Suave\'s own list. Swipe left on the 123 or ABC key to open it. The current system clip is also shown there even before it is stored.
On - stays visible even while a physical keyboard is connected
Off - hides itself while a physical keyboard is connected
On - a bar above the keyboard shows the last install time, the focused app, and that app\'s editor capabilities
Off - the keyboard has no debug bar
The install time is read from the APK at runtime so you can confirm a fresh install actually took effect. The rest names the app currently focused and how its text field was classified.
